title: Prague Tram Peak Fleet
description: Network as of Sunday 27 Sep 2026 (line 2 on the long route to Náměstí Bratří Synků, line 23 switched to Královka – Bílá labuť); vehicles from the Friday 25 Sep afternoon peak, with line 2 resized to its long-route 12 courses.

gtfs._why: first weekday on the 27 Sep network; 28 Sep is a public holiday. The feed of 28 Sep starts that day, so it cannot give 25 Sep.

5/6.note: Shared pool, modelled as one Simutrans line. This is the user's modelling choice (pools are preferred for 5/6), not what the records show: in reality 19 of the 25 courses run through. Lines 5 and 6 share one pool of courses numbered as line 5 and both end at Nádraží Holešovice (courses that switch are marked →6). The Simutrans line runs Slivenec → Nádraží Holešovice → Kubánské náměstí → Nádraží Holešovice → Slivenec. The tram changes its number at Nádraží Holešovice, a through stop with no loop, so the real minute is kept. The real timetable pairs arrivals and departures there in the same minute, so each tram waits about 8 minutes for its next slot; with Leave up to on auto, nothing queues.

transfers.note: Course 22/42. The record says it moves to line 7 (přejezd na linku 7). Line 7 has afternoon trips starting at Hotel Golf and an evening run to Strašnice depot, which fits a 22 morning / 7 afternoon course.

added_courses.note: Added for the long route. Line 2 ran courses 1–12 on the long route (9–11 Sep) but only 1–10 on the short Albertov route on 25 Sep. This set ran 2/11 on Fri 11 Sep and was not in service on 25 Sep. 2/11 is a Strašnice course with a Tatra T3 pair every day.

Added for the long route. 2/12 is a Pankrác Škoda 15T course (afternoon part: 9234 on 11 Sep, 9349 on 10 Sep, 9211 on 9 Sep). All three were busy on other lines on 25 Sep, so this is a designed stand-in, not recorded: 9229, a Pankrác 15T3 in service and unused that day.

course_notes.1/8: 9328 had first run 20/17 until it was replaced there by 9228.

2: Resized for the long route Sídliště Petřiny – Náměstí Bratří Synků. On Fri 25 Sep line 2 still ran short to Albertov with courses 1–10 (shown as recorded). Courses 11 and 12 are added from the long-route days 9–11 Sep, as their notes say.
13: Only course 13/1 is recorded, on every day of the last two weeks. The timetable needs 4 sets at 16:00 (every 8 min, 12–13 min each way, at least 3 min turnaround at each end), so courses 13/2–13/4 are designed, not recorded: single Tatra T3R.PLF cars from Strašnice that ran line 13 on other days and were not used anywhere on 25 Sep.
31: Only courses 31/1–3 are recorded, on every day of the last two weeks. The timetable needs 5 sets at 16:00 (every 8 min, 18–20 min each way, with the timetable's own 1-minute turnaround at Vysočanská), so courses 31/4–31/5 are designed, not recorded: single Tatra T3R.PLF cars from Hloubětín that ran line 31 on the dates given and were not used anywhere on 25 Sep.
23: Nostalgic PID line with museum cars. It already ran the switched route Královka – Bílá labuť on 25 Sep (since 19 Sep) with its usual 4 courses, the same number as on the old Zvonařka route (9–11 Sep), so no resizing is needed.
7: Course 22/42 (8314 + 8315) is listed here because its record says it moves to line 7. The time of the move is not recorded.
22: Line 22 runs as two separate branches, and each is its own Simutrans line. The records do not say which course runs which branch, so the split below is a choice: both branches need 17 sets by round trip, and the 40 courses are shared out evenly.
17: Line 17 runs as two branches, each its own Simutrans line. Here the course numbers mark the branch: 17/1–17 (all bidirectional Tatra KT8D5.RN2P) run Březiněveská – Libuš, where the temporary stub needs bidirectional trams, and 17/21–37 run Vozovna Kobylisy – Levského. Each branch needs 15 sets by round trip; 17 are recorded on each.

depot_notes.Střešovice: Museum depot. Historic cars for lines 23 and 42.

17.label: 17 Březiněveská – Libuš
17.why: Courses 17/1–17 are all bidirectional Tatra KT8D5.RN2P, which the temporary stub at Libuš needs.

17.label: 17 Vozovna Kobylisy – Levského
17.why: Courses 17/21–37 are single-direction sets (Tatra T3 pairs, Škoda 14T and 15T), which need the loops at Vozovna Kobylisy and Levského.

22.label: 22 Bílá Hora – Zahradní Město
22.why: Not recorded: the records give no branch. Both branches need 17 sets by round trip; the 40 courses are split evenly in course order, with the 6 spares shared (35–37 here).

22.label: 22 Nádraží Hostivař – Vypich
22.why: Not recorded: a choice, as for the other branch; the peak extras 41, 43 and 44 are placed here (42 moves to line 7).

turnaround_min._why: Brno review: at Vysočanská the timetable itself turns trams in 1 min; the default 3-min minimum inflated the need (7 instead of 5).

metro._why: user, 28 Sep: 'Prague needs also a metro mention. I need intervals, lines and number of trains. One summary table at the bottom is enough.'
metro._stock_source: dpp.cz/vozovy-park/metro/81-71m; cs.wikipedia 'Metro v Praze' (Brno session review, 28 Sep: A runs 81-71M, not M1)
metro._reverse_why: All metro termini reverse behind the station; the timetable does not show the reversing time, so the need is given for 3–5 min (Brno review asked for per-terminus turnarounds; the timetable's arrival→next departure there is a different train, 0–1 min).

ferry._why: user, 29 Sep: 'Keep the separate files bus only, add ferries to the tram/metro one'. PID ferries (route type 4) summarised like the metro.
ferry._turn_why: The timetable turns the boat round at the pier in the minute it lands (P4: Dostihová 16:00 → Belárie 16:02, back 16:02), so boats are sized with 0 min at the pier.
